- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +0.23) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate when sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -0.11 or -0.16) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lag in response to recent price drops — model often holds too high for 1–2 days after a dip.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, underestimating long-term trend reversion.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid assuming momentum — sentiment history should be weighted more heavily than recent price action.
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., +0.23) in last 3–5 days, model should not over-forecast beyond +5% above recent high.
- If sentiment is negative for 5+ consecutive days, model should not forecast >1% above prior 18-day average — avoid bullish false signals.
- Correct for “sentiment lag” — if sentiment turned positive 2–3 days ago, model should not yet reflect full price rise.
